job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
KC Group is working with a growing SME with a group of businesses across multiple sectors, entering an exciting phase of expansion. As a result, they are looking to appoint a Finance Manager to take ownership of the finance function and help build the financial infrastructure needed to support continued growth. This is a high-impact role working closely with the Managing Director, offering genuine scope to shape the finance function and progress into a Financial Controller position over time.

This position will evolve the finance function from a primarily transactional and compliance-based environment into a forward-looking, insight-driven function. You will introduce improved reporting, budgeting and forecasting to support strategic decision-making as the business scales.

Key Responsibilities

You will take overall ownership of the finance function, leading and developing a small team while acting as a key business partner to the Managing Director and wider leadership team. This will involve collaborating closely with operational, sales and purchasing teams, as well as managing relationships with external advisors and banking partners. You will be responsible for delivering accurate and timely financial reporting, including full monthly management accounts with clear commentary on performance, risks and opportunities. Maintaining strong financial control across the balance sheet, ensuring compliance with statutory requirements, and supporting quarterly reporting obligations will form a key part of the role.

A core focus will be improving cash flow visibility and working capital management, through the development of rolling forecasts, monitoring stock and debtor positions, and proactively identifying risks to liquidity while supporting informed decision-making. You will also introduce and lead structured budgeting and forecasting processes, delivering annual budgets, rolling forecasts and variance analysis, while building financial models to support strategic planning and translating financial data into clear insight for non-finance stakeholders.

From a commercial perspective, you will provide valuable analysis on margins, pricing and profitability, supporting supplier negotiations, monitoring cost of goods and identifying opportunities to improve financial performance, as well as contributing to new product launches and growth initiatives. Alongside this, you will play a key role in strengthening systems and processes, improving reporting tools and data visibility, enhancing financial controls appropriate for a growing SME, and supporting the implementation of the Unleashed inventory system alongside existing Xero systems.

About You

  • Experience within product-based, manufacturing, FMCG or stock-led environments would be advantageous.
  • Qualified (ACA/ACCA/CIMA), part-qualified or strong QBE candidates will all be considered.
  • Experience as a Finance Manager, Financial Controller or similar
  • Background in a growing SME or entrepreneurial environment
  • Strong management accounts, forecasting and budgeting experience
  • Comfortable building processes in a scaling business
  • Able to communicate financial information to non-finance stakeholders
  • Commercially minded with the ability to influence decision-making


You’ll be joining a fast-paced, entrepreneurial business where ideas are encouraged, ownership is valued, and you can make a real impact. This is a fantastic opportunity to work closely with leadership and shape the future of the finance function.

Benefits include:

  • 33 days holiday (including bank holidays)
  • Flexible working hours (core hours 10:00am – 4:30pm)
  • Clear progression to Financial Controller
  • Collaborative and supportive team environment

job.title: Neighbourhood Manager
job.description:
KC Group are recruiting on behalf of a leading housing organisation for a Neighbourhood Manager, In the Stratford Upon Avon area.

Please note that an Enhanced DBS check is required for this role. Candidates must either hold a valid Enhanced DBS certificate or be registered with the DBS Update Service.

This is a full-time temporary role, Monday-Friday, 37.5 hours per week, paying £22.25 per hour.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established housing provider where you'll act as the face of the organisation across a designated patch, supporting customers to create safe, sustainable, and thriving communities. You will take ownership of the end-to-end customer experience, working closely with residents, contractors, local agencies, and internal departments to deliver outstanding neighbourhood services.

Key Responsibilities Neighbourhood Manager:

  • Manage a portfolio of residential and mixed-tenure properties across the Thanet area.
  • Conduct estate, property, and scheme inspections to maintain high standards.
  • Support customers with tenancy management matters including tenancy changes, succession, safeguarding, and enforcement cases.
  • Investigate and manage anti-social behaviour, community safety concerns, and complaints.
  • Build strong relationships with customers, external agencies, and local stakeholders.
  • Work closely with contractors and internal teams to resolve maintenance and compliance issues.
  • Attend community meetings, customer engagement events, and multi-agency meetings where required.
  • Maintain accurate records and update housing management systems.

To be considered for the Neighbourhood Manager:

  • Previous experience within housing, tenancy management, or neighbourhood management.
  • Strong customer service and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and conflict-resolution abilities.
  • Knowledge of housing legislation and tenancy processes is desirable.
  • Confident using Microsoft Office and mobile technology.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage a varied workload.
  • Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle insured for business use.

Key Information Neighbourhood Manager role:

  • £22.25 per hour.
  • Full-time temporary assignment.
  • Field-based role covering Thanet and surrounding communities.
  • Opportunity to work for a respected social housing organisation.
  • Hybrid working with regular community and estate visits.
  • Immediate start available.

For more information on the role, contact Reiss on reiss@kateandco.com or 0121 705 0077. Unsuccessful applications will be kept on file for future vacancies.

job.title: Recruitment Partner
job.description:
Following a highly successful year, including securing three national recruitment frameworks, KC Group is continuing to grow and is looking to appoint experienced Recruitment Partners across the following divisions:

�� Business Support
�� Human Resources
�� Accountancy & Finance

We're looking for experienced recruiters who are passionate about building lasting relationships and take real satisfaction in matching the right people with the right opportunities. You'll have the autonomy to develop and manage your own market, supported by an established business that values long-term success over short-term gains.

Key Responsibilities of the Recruitment Partner role:

  • Managing the full recruitment lifecycle, from client brief through to successful placement
  • Developing new business opportunities and building long-term client relationships within your specialist market
  • Growing and maintaining a strong network of candidates, becoming a trusted career partner
  • Delivering consultative, high-quality recruitment solutions
  • Leveraging KC Group's respected brand, established client base and national framework agreements
  • Building a sustainable, relationship-led desk driven by repeat and retained business
  • Supporting and mentoring junior team members as the business grows
  • Creating and executing effective business development strategies

About You

  • Previous recruitment agency experience
  • A proven track record of billing and/or business development success
  • A consultative, relationship-focused approach with the ability to build trust and credibility
  • Commercial awareness, self-motivation and a strong desire to succeed
  • Ambitious, resilient and excited by the opportunity to contribute to a growing business

What's on Offer

  • Competitive basic salary with uncapped commission
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
  • Genuine autonomy, trust and support
  • Generous annual leave entitlement, plus:An additional day off for your birthday
  • Four dedicated wellbeing days each year
  • Access to the BHSF Benefits Portal, including:Digital GP access
  • Counselling and wellbeing support
  • Hundreds of retail, leisure and hospitality discounts
  • Quarterly incentives, including team away days and overseas trips
  • Opportunity to work on national frameworks and established client accounts
  • Clear progression pathways into senior and leadership roles
  • Supportive and experienced leadership team

For more Information, get in touch on 0121 705 0077 or click apply and a member of our team will be In touch as soon as possible.

Why KC Group? Founded in 1997, KC Group has built its reputation on quality, integrity and long-term partnerships with both clients and candidates. Following a standout year of growth, multiple national framework wins and ambitious plans for the future, there has never been a better time to join the business and play a key role in the next stage of our journey.

job.title: Direct Tax Assistant Manager
job.description:
Corporate Tax | First Move into Industry | £Competitive | Cheshire

Recently qualified in Tax and ready to make your first move into industry?

KC Group are working with a high-growth, global business that is looking to hire a newly qualified Corporate Tax professional into its growing in-house tax team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone coming from a Top 6 accountancy firm with strong corporate tax compliance experience who wants to move into industry and gain exposure to much more than compliance.

You’ll work closely with the Head of Direct Tax and Direct Tax Manager, supporting a broad UK and international tax agenda across compliance, tax accounting, transfer pricing and wider advisory projects.

What will you be doing?

  • Take responsibility for the UK corporation tax compliance process across approximately 40 legal entities
  • Prepare corporation tax computations for the group's larger companies
  • Support tax accounting, deferred tax and tax disclosures
  • Review overseas corporation tax returns prepared by external providers
  • Calculate UK corporation tax payments using business forecasts
  • Support Corporate Interest Restriction calculations
  • Manage withholding tax treaty claims relating to interest and dividends
  • Assist with overseas tax payment tracking
  • Deal with corporation tax enquiries from tax authorities
  • Get involved in internal restructures, R&D/RDEC claims and capital allowances projects
  • Support the preparation and maintenance of UK transfer pricing documentation
  • Help develop and improve a more modern, scalable corporate tax compliance process

What are they looking for? Ideally, you'll be:

  • ACA / CTA / ATT qualified
  • Trained within a Top 6 accountancy firm
  • Experienced in corporate tax compliance, ideally across groups
  • Comfortable with tax accounting
  • Strong technically with excellent attention to detail
  • Confident using Excel and tax preparation software — Alphatax experience is particularly useful
  • A strong communicator who can build relationships with both Finance and wider business teams
  • Someone who enjoys responsibility, problem solving and continuous improvement

job.title: Sales Support Coordinator
job.description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Sales Support Coordinator to join a well-established and highly regarded organisation based in Birmingham.

As part of the role, you will provide comprehensive administrative support to the sales team while delivering a high standard of customer service to external clients. This is a varied role that would suit someone who is organised, commercially aware and confident working across multiple systems and priorities.

Key Responsibilities as a Sales Support Coordinator:

  • Answer incoming calls and deal with general customer enquiries professionally and efficiently.
  • Process sample requests from architects, contractors and other customers, including requests received via the website.
  • Liaise with suppliers to arrange samples and monitor deliveries, keeping the relevant sales team members updated.
  • Maintain and review sample reports to identify and monitor new business opportunities.
  • Prepare customer quotations, including initial pricing and revised or duplicated quotations.
  • Create and maintain product information and pricing records across internal systems.
  • Arrange product testing and obtain relevant certification and documentation when required.
  • Process project registrations and reservations on behalf of the sales team.
  • Provide product-specific technical information and data sheets to customers and colleagues.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer and project information within the CRM system.
  • Use Microsoft Teams and other internal systems to organise and maintain project-related sales information.
  • Prepare professional emails, letters and other correspondence as required.
  • Work closely with both internal and external sales teams to ensure enquiries and customer requirements are dealt with promptly.

The ideal candidate will have the following experience:

  • Previous experience in a sales support, sales administration or similar administrative role.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organisational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
  • A proactive and positive approach to work.
  • The ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines effectively.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • A high level of professionalism, integrity and accountability.
  • Experience working with CRM or business management systems.
  • Previous SAP experience would be advantageous, although full training can be provided.

If you are an organised and commercially focused administrator looking for a new opportunity within a supportive and professional sales environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

If your CV is not shortlisted for this role, we will keep your CV on file for future opportunities.

job.title: Business Validation Analyst
job.description:
IMMEDIATE START REQUIRED

We are recruiting for a number of Business Validation Analysts to support a large-scale business verification project. Please note, this role requires a Basic DBS and Is Initially a 4-6 week assignment with potential for extension and permanent opportunities.

This is a full-time, temporary, fully remote opportunity and is ideal for candidates with experience in merchant onboarding, KYB/KYC, financial crime, underwriting, credit risk, compliance, fraud investigations or business research.

You will be responsible for validating businesses through online research, reviewing company records, websites, ownership structures and independent sources to ensure organisations are legitimate and accurately represented.

Key duties of the Business Validation Analyst role include:

  • Conducting business verification, KYB and KYC checks
  • Reviewing company records, websites and supporting documentation
  • Carrying out sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening
  • Investigating discrepancies and identifying potential risks
  • Conducting research using multiple online data sources
  • Recording clear, evidence-based decisions and findings
  • Escalating complex cases where required

Ideal candidates for the Business Validation Analyst role will have experience in:

  • Merchant onboarding or underwriting
  • KYB/KYC, AML or financial crime investigations
  • Credit risk or business information analysis
  • Compliance, fraud or intelligence research
  • Strong administrative or research-based roles with excellent attention to detail

To be considered for the Business Validation Analyst role, you will need:

  • Excellent online research skills
  • Strong written communication
  • Sound judgement and analytical thinking
  • A high level of accuracy and attention to detail
  • Confidence working independently in a remote environment

Key Information:

  • Fully remote, UK-based role
  • Initial 4-6 week assignment with potential for extension and permanent opportunities
  • £17.00 per hour
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week
  • Flexible working patterns available
  • Own laptop and reliable internet connection required
  • French or German language skills would be advantageous but are not essential
